questions.s:

Rule / Concept: Use of "Each" -

The distributive pronoun "Each" is always considered a singular subject. When a sentence follows the structure "Each of + Plural Noun," the plural noun is simply part of a prepositional phrase. The verb must ignore that plural noun and agree with "Each."

Analysis of the Complexity - This question is a "double-trap" because it contains two different verbs that look like they might be errors, but only one is.

This is CORRECT. The word "who" refers back to "researchers" (plural). Therefore, the verb inside this specific clause must be plural.

This is INCORRECT. This verb belongs to the subject "Each." Because "Each" is singular, the verb must be "was asked."

Corrected Sentence - Each of the senior researchers who were painstakingly assigned to the multi-disciplinary international climate project was asked to submit his findings by the end of the quarter.

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The small cafe at the end of the road is her.
questions.s:
The correct answer is- is her.

Key Points​​

  • Subjective pronouns (he, she, it) are used as the subject whereas objective pronouns (him, her, itself) are used as the object of the sentence.
  • Possessive pronouns show that something belongs to someone.
  • The possessive pronouns are: my, our, your, his, her, its, and their.
  • There’s also an independent form of each of these pronouns: mine, ours, yours, his, hers, its, and theirs.
  • Independent possessive pronouns (also called absolute possessive pronouns) must be used without a noun.
  • ​Example:
    • The book is my.
    • The book is mine.
  • ​As per the rule given above, 'hers' will be used instead of 'her' in the 2nd part of the sentence.
     

​​Correct Sentence: The small cafe at the end of the road is hers.

​​​Additional Information   ​

  • ​​Possessive pronouns can be used as the object of a preposition.
  • Example:
    • My house is better than your.
    • My house is better than yours.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

The CEO, wanting to avoid any legal complications, insisted that his team let the lawyer and I handle the sensitive negotiations with the disgruntled former employee.
o: let the lawyer and me handle
lets the lawyer and I handle
let the lawyer and myself handle
questions.s:
The error is in the pronoun case following the verb "let". The verb "let" is always followed by a pronoun in the objective case (me, you, him, her, us, them). Here, the subject pronoun "I" is incorrectly used.

· Option a) "let the lawyer and me handle" is correct. It uses the object pronoun "me" after the verb "let", which is the grammatically correct form.

· Option b) "lets the lawyer and I handle" is incorrect for two reasons: it uses the singular verb "lets" which doesn't fit the subjunctive mood here, and it uses the incorrect subject pronoun "I".

· Option c) "let the lawyer and myself handle" is incorrect because the reflexive pronoun "myself" cannot be used as a simple object of a verb like "let".

· Option d) 'No substitution' is incorrect because the original phrase uses the wrong pronoun case.

So, the correct sentence is: The CEO, wanting to avoid any legal complications, insisted that his team let the lawyer and me handle the sensitive negotiations with the disgruntled former employee.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
